faqItems.q: Is it hard to set up?
faqItems.a: No. Upload your video, choose when it runs, and add your CTA — ready to publish in minutes, no technical skills needed.

faqItems.q: Do I have to be there when someone watches it?
faqItems.a: No. Once published, the webinar runs on its own: registration, waiting room, playback, chat, and CTAs all work without anyone on your end connected.

faqItems.q: Can I use a presentation I already recorded?
faqItems.a: Yes. If you already have a video (on YouTube, Vimeo, or a direct link), just connect it — no need to record again.

faqItems.q: Can I connect my other tools?
faqItems.a: Yes, from the Pro plan up. WeWebinars connects to your CRM, email marketing, or automation via direct integrations or webhooks.

faqItems.q: Does this work for my kind of business?
faqItems.a: If you present the same thing more than once to sell — a demo, a talk, a pitch — it works. The industry doesn't matter.

faqItems.q: What's the difference from just sharing a recording?
faqItems.a: A recording only plays back. WeWebinars adds registration, scheduling, chat, CTAs at just the right moment, and analytics on what's working — around that same video.

faqItems.q: Why automate instead of just presenting live?
faqItems.a: Because your presentation keeps selling while you do anything else — and whoever's watching still gets an experience with real pacing and response, not a loose recording.

faqItems.q: Which plan do I need to start?
faqItems.a: Starter is enough to automate your first presentation. Most people using it seriously end up on Pro, for the active webinars and the AI Chat Agent.

faqItems.q: Can I start small and grow later?
faqItems.a: Yes — switch plans whenever you need to, without losing anything you've already set up.

faqItems.q: What if someone wants to talk to a real person?
faqItems.a: Your CTAs can lead to booking a call, messaging you on WhatsApp, or going straight to checkout — you decide the next step.

blueprint.title: 18-Slide Blueprint
blueprint.subtitle: Walk through your webinar's full architecture, act by act.
blueprint.notesPlaceholder: How would you apply this slide to your presentation?

problem.title: Act I: The problem
problem.description: Make the limitation of the current approach visible and create relevance.

new_way.title: Act II: The new way
new_way.description: Shift the audience's belief and introduce a new paradigm.

criteria.title: Act III: The criteria
criteria.description: Show what an effective solution must meet.

implementation.title: Act IV: The implementation
implementation.description: Present the vehicle, the offer, and the next step.

slide1.title: Cover / Big idea
slide1.objective: Capture immediate attention and create genuine curiosity before explaining anything.
slide1.question: What question or tension makes someone want to keep watching the next 30 seconds?
slide1.example: "What if you could sell without being present on every call?"
slide1.visualTip: One large sentence, no logos or secondary text competing for attention.

slide2.title: Identification
slide2.objective: Get the audience to recognize themselves in the situation described.
slide2.question: How would you describe your audience's current situation in their own words?
slide2.example: "If you repeat the same demo every week and feel your time isn't paying off..."
slide2.visualTip: An image or icon representing the person, not the product.

slide3.title: The hidden cost
slide3.objective: Make tangible what the current way of doing things is costing in time, money, or energy.
slide3.question: How much is it costing your audience to keep doing things the way they do today?
slide3.example: "Every repeated presentation is 2 hours that don't come back."
slide3.visualTip: A concrete number or figure, not a vague statement.

slide4.title: The false problem
slide4.objective: Question the surface-level explanation the audience already gave themselves.
slide4.question: What obvious solution have they already tried that doesn't actually address the real cause?
slide4.example: "Hiring more people doesn't fix a process that depends on one single person."
slide4.visualTip: Visually contrast "what looks like the problem" against what follows.

slide5.title: The real cause
slide5.objective: Reveal the true bottleneck behind the symptom.
slide5.question: What's the root cause nobody had pointed out to them before?
slide5.example: "The problem isn't the presentation. It's that its delivery depends on your time."
slide5.visualTip: A simple diagram showing cause → symptom, not just text.

slide6.title: Paradigm shift
slide6.objective: Install a new way of seeing the problem that makes the solution that follows obvious.
slide6.question: What does your audience believe today that they need to stop believing?
slide6.example: "Selling isn't an innate skill, it's a repeatable system."
slide6.visualTip: Conceptual before/after, not the product yet.

slide7.title: The mechanism
slide7.objective: Explain how the new way works without presenting the product yet.
slide7.question: What are the concrete steps that make this work?
slide7.visualTip: A numbered sequence of 3 to 5 steps, simple and visual.

slide8.title: Before vs. after
slide8.objective: Contrast the current system with the new possible reality.
slide8.question: What does day-to-day look like before and after adopting this mechanism?
slide8.example: "Before: 5 identical calls a week. After: 1 presentation that works on its own."
slide8.visualTip: Side-by-side table or columns, few words per row.

slide9.title: The right experience
slide9.objective: Define how a well-built solution should feel or work.
slide9.question: What would someone expect to experience if this worked exactly as it should?
slide9.example: "It should feel as personal as a 1:1 call, without you being there."
slide9.visualTip: Sensory language: how it looks, feels, how long it takes.

slide10.title: The criteria
slide10.objective: Establish the objective criteria any good solution should meet.
slide10.question: What would a solution absolutely have to meet for you to trust it?
slide10.example: "It has to work without my presence, measure results, and look professional."
slide10.visualTip: A checklist of 3 to 5 criteria, not a paragraph.

slide11.title: Capture and registration
slide11.objective: Show how the journey begins for someone who arrives at the solution.
slide11.question: What's the first thing someone does to start using this?
slide11.example: "They register on a page with a single clear promise."
slide11.visualTip: A screenshot or simplified mockup of the first step.

slide12.title: The experience itself
slide12.objective: Show what the person lives through during the core experience.
slide12.question: What happens during the main moment of the experience?
slide12.example: "They watch the recorded presentation as if it were live, on their own schedule."
slide12.visualTip: A capture of the real experience, not a generic illustration.

slide13.title: Conversation and attention
slide13.objective: Show how questions get answered and buying intent gets detected.
slide13.question: How does the person know they can ask a question and get an answer?
slide13.example: "A live chat answers questions while they watch the presentation."
slide13.visualTip: A real example of a question and answer, not an abstract description.

slide14.title: CTA at the right moment
slide14.objective: Connect the presentation to a relevant action at the right time.
slide14.question: At exactly what moment does the invitation to act appear?
slide14.example: "The booking button appears only after explaining the mechanism."
slide14.visualTip: Mark on a timeline where the CTA appears.

slide15.title: Data to improve
slide15.objective: Show how the process gets measured and optimized over time.
slide15.question: What data lets someone know whether this is working?
slide15.example: "How many registered, how many watched fully, how many took action."
slide15.visualTip: A simple panel or 3 key metrics, not a full table.

slide16.title: Presenting the solution
slide16.objective: Reveal the product as the natural consequence of everything explained before.
slide16.question: How is the offer presented so it feels like the logical next step, not a sales pitch?
slide16.example: "That's why we built [product]: the system that does exactly this for you."
slide16.visualTip: The first moment where the product is shown with a name and clear shape.

slide17.title: Offer and choice
slide17.objective: Clearly communicate what the person gets, at what price, and with what guarantees.
slide17.question: What exactly does the offer include, and what lowers the risk of saying yes?
slide17.example: "It includes X, Y, Z. 30-day guarantee. Clear price and payment terms."
slide17.visualTip: A list of what's included plus the price, no hidden fine print.

slide18.title: Decision / CTA
slide18.objective: Close with a single clear instruction, no ambiguity or multiple paths.
slide18.question: What's the one action you're asking the audience to take right now?
slide18.example: "Book your call below. It's the only button on this page."
slide18.visualTip: One single button, one message, no visual competition.

why_evergreen.title: Why go evergreen
why_evergreen.body: Every time you repeat your presentation live, that time disappears the moment the call ends. An evergreen webinar flips that logic: you record it once, set it up once, and that same presentation keeps working 24/7 without you having to be there. The difference isn't just about time -- your presentation goes from being an event you organize every week to an asset that keeps selling while you do something else.

the_four_acts.title: The 4 acts of your script
the_four_acts.body: Every evergreen webinar that converts follows the same 18-slide narrative structure, organized into 4 acts:

launch_checklist.title: Launch checklist
launch_checklist.body: Before you publish, make sure you have these 6 pieces ready -- they're exactly the sections of the WeWebinars wizard:

common_mistakes.title: Common mistakes when going evergreen
common_mistakes.body:
- Recording the presentation exactly as you give it live, without adapting the script for someone watching without you there to answer questions.
- Jumping straight to recording without going through the Blueprint: the result sounds like a product pitch, not a story that leads to a decision.
- Not scheduling CTAs or simulated chat -- a video with no interaction at all feels recorded, not live.
- Launching without testing the full registration, waiting room, and live room flow from a first-time visitor's point of view.
